message.content: The 19th‑century sculpture that most people think of when they hear “famous” is **Auguste Rodin’s “The Kiss” (1889)**.  It was the first of Rodin’s works to be widely celebrated in its own right (before his later “The Thinker” and “The Gates of Hell” became iconic).  “The Kiss” captured the era’s fascination with realism, emotion, and the human form, and it remains one of the most reproduced and admired sculptures from that period.
